title: An optimized confocal intravital microscopy protocol for long-term live imaging of murine F-actin organization during naïve lymphocyte migration
protocol: Anesthetize the recipient host C57BL/6J mouse by intraperitoneal injection of Avertin (300 mg/kg).
Cut away skin and gently expose the femoral vein.
Inject fluorescent-labeled lymphocytes into the femoral vein using insulin syringe with 30G needle, under the dissecting microscope.
Seal the needle wound with a cautery pen or apply pressure on the wound with Q-tip to stop bleeding.
Cover the open skin area with a strip of surgical tape.
Return the anesthetized mouse to a heated incubator (∼30°C–37°C) to maintain physiological temperature before lymph node surgery.
Remove the anesthetized mouse from the incubator.
Determine if the mouse is fully sedated by lack of response to toe and/or tail pinches.
Inject half dose of initial Avertin injection if necessary.
Inject fluorescently labeled antibodies (i.e., CD31-Alexa Fluor 647) via retro-orbital injection.
Use an electric trimmer to remove hair on the abdominal area of the mouse.
Remove remaining loose hair by alcohol swab and gently patting the area with tape.
Place the mouse on a clear surgical board in a supine position.
Stabilize the mouse to the board with taping each footpad to the board.
Place the mouse under the dissecting microscope.
Make a midline incision along the ventral surface of the abdominal cavity using surgical scissors.
Gently retract the skin away from the flesh to expose the tissue.
Keep the exposed tissue moist with gauze dampened with PBS throughout the procedure.
Stabilize the edges of the retracted skin with surgical tape once the inguinal lymph node is visible.
Carefully remove the thin layer of connective tissue covering the area around the lymph node using fine forceps and micro-scissors.
Clear the adipose tissue covering and surrounding the lymph node.
Avoid contact with the vasculature during the procedure to prevent injury.
Place the mouse under the confocal microscope for imaging.
Obtain optimal imaging insert best suited for the microscope stage.
Cover the imaging insert with Corning cover glass.
Gently flip the mouse upside down under the dissecting microscope.
Secure the preparation onto an imaging stage.
Maneuver the skin flap so that the lymph node is at the middle of the slide.
Tape the skin flap firmly to the cover glass, ensuring all corners are securely attached.
Place a few droplets of 1× PBS on the cover slip between the lymph node and glass.
Switch on the confocal microscope, lasers, and computers.
Allow the lasers and lamps to warm up.
Place the mouse preparation on the microscope stage.
Identify the lymph node and vasculature using wide-field settings on the microscope.
Switch to confocal mode.
Set up 4D imaging acquisition parameters.
Choose laser settings based on excitation/emission wavelengths of the fluorochromes used.
Adjust intensity parameters such as gain and pinhole.
Set time-lapse parameter settings for desired frame rate (∼30 – 60 sec per interval).
Acquire overall duration (∼30 – 60 min) for imaging.
Inject half dose of initial Avertin every 1–1.5 hours to maintain mouse under anesthesia.
Firmly stabilize the skin flap with surgical tape during time-lapse acquisition to avoid z-plane scan field shifts.
Use analysis software to correct any shifts in the scan field during initial time-lapse image acquisition.
Create 4D reconstructions from the acquired raw data using appropriate software such as Imaris.
